notes: Section 9 (Bayview / Islais Creek, both sides of Third St): chosen because all six legend patterns meet here: heavy industrial (square grid, top-left), unrestricted (checkerboard, north-east), light industrial (fine crosshatch, centre), first residential (diagonal, south-east), second residential (white blocks, left) and commercial (solid black frontage along Third St). Box kept east of the two railway lines (x < 1555 at y 2080). JUDGMENT CALLS FOR THE OWNER: (1) The dashed line (1951,2080)-(2199,2285) is read as the unbuilt north-east side of Arthur Ave; the land north-east of it (bay/marsh, no outline) is marked open, with a limit along the dashes (no label on the line). (2) Several checkerboard blocks carry a thin outlined white strip along one side or end (lots of another district), read as part of the block they lie along. Where a strip's line touches the next block across a narrow street the two are cut apart with short limits (no label): (1785,2213)-(1792,2195), (1906,2272)-(1922,2258), (2022,2349)-(2036,2335), (2026,2405)-(2042,2416), (2076,2521)-(2087,2506). The strip along the north-east side of the block at about (1865,2233) (strip 1870-1928, 2198-2265) is open to the street at one end, so its inside is labelled street; it may belong to the block. (3) Two checkerboard blocks touch at both corners of a small white square at (1950-1971, 2263-2283): read as the street running between them; limits across the two pinches, (1945,2268)-(1953,2275) and (1961,2280)-(1969,2287), and a street seed in the square. (4) The black triangles in Third St at about (1658,2156) and (1611,2388) are read as small commercial blocks. (5) The black wedge at (1615-1657, 2317-2372) has a thin white strip inside its outline open at the bottom; closed with a stroke (1636,2367)-(1632,2373) so the strip is part of the block. (6) The lettering ARTHUR at (1940,2090) and small dots in the streets are left unseeded (street). Blocks cut by the box sides are seeded where they show (e.g. 1857,2089; 2197,2376; 1567,2657; 1565,2424).
